payload.adrs:
FIVE NODES MINTED THIS PASS, four decisions and one risk. Each addresses the requirement or quality that forced it; rejected options stay recorded as history rather than being deleted.

se.adr-search-is-two-jobs — ADDRESSES R3, R5, C1, C4, C9. SUPERSEDES se.adr-git-is-the-only-searcher.
Searching the working tree and searching the record are two jobs; each gets the provider that fits. The deciding argument is recorded as the SHAPE OF EACH FAILURE rather than the score, because the margin was narrow: the rival fails silently and late (our parser reading two output shapes, one of which packs two identifiers into a single field), while the chosen design fails loudly and once (a package either resolves a per-platform binary at install or it does not). What it costs is stated rather than minimised — the rival was BETTER on the owner's standing one-click bar.
REJECTED AND KEPT: the single-provider design, explicitly as a viable fallback with its capabilities probed, not as a straw man. Also the hybrid with a fallback path, rejected because it keeps two implementations for one question and an untested fallback is code we never run.

se.adr-rounds-are-injected-at-the-compiler — ADDRESSES R30, need N10, goal G5.
The four rounds are appended where evidence forms are built, as required fields, at one place. The record carries the reason it had to be structural: the rounds were required in writing since the method note was authored, no form ever asked, and not one had been filled in any gate of any iteration while every one of those gates went green.
REJECTED AND KEPT: hand-authoring per gate (one edit forever, and a later gate simply misses them — which is how the omission arose); a lint that complains afterwards (detects rather than prevents, and an unattended run has moved on); a separate review sub-machine (changes the machine's shape, which this iteration's excluded list forbids — recorded as the natural successor if entry criteria are ever added).

se.adr-reopen-supersedes-and-rearms — ADDRESSES R31, need N11.
A reopen re-activates the named states and their cone, supersedes rather than deletes, and leaves every downstream join reachable. The third clause carries both engine defects that produced it: the first live reopen stranded a three-way join and the walk stopped in silence; the fix for that handed fuel back for the states it was activating, so they re-activated themselves and the walk again never moved.
REJECTED AND KEPT: abandon-and-restart (destroys the record of what was believed, which is the one thing a reopen is for); hand-editing the instance (an out-of-lane write this project has already paid for).

se.adr-engine-promotes-to-trunk — ADDRESSES R33, R34, tension T2.
Engine changes land on trunk from an open iteration under four enforced rules. The record carries why the obvious alternative fails — a per-worktree engine means parallel agents are judged by different machines and a gate stops meaning one thing — and the honest cost: engine code reaches trunk before its own gates have reviewed it, so the suite is the guard, which is why an empty verification run must count as FAILED.
KNOWN LIMIT RECORDED IN THE NODE: the promotion runs trunk's copy of its own code, so a fix to the promotion cannot be delivered by the promotion.

se.raid-a-recorded-decision-did-not-reach-the-state-that-contradicted-it — the finding of this state, and it is uncomfortable enough to belong in the ledger rather than in a note.
WHAT HAPPENED: this iteration's FIRST pass recorded se.adr-untracked-files-are-searched-by-default, which states plainly that version-control grep is tracked-files-only by default, that a just-written file would therefore be invisible, and that the flag exists. Two hours later the SAME iteration's rewalk eliminated a candidate on the claim that version-control grep cannot see an unstaged file — contradicting a decision it had itself recorded, about the same tool, within one working session. The red-team round caught it by probe, and the probe RE-DISCOVERED what the ledger already said.
WHY IT IS RECORDED HERE: the comfortable reading is 'the red team worked', and it did. The accurate reading is that a decision already in the ledger did not reach the state that contradicted it. If a decision recorded two hours ago cannot reach the state it binds, no rule minted last month will either — which is R14's entire case, demonstrated by this iteration on itself, for the second time.
CONSEQUENCE: R14's join must cover DECISION nodes, not only guidance and laws. That is a second, independent reason the applicability migration is not optional.

NOT RE-MINTED, because the first pass's nodes stand and the why lives once: se.adr-untracked-files-are-searched-by-default (the working-tree default is inverted at our boundary, so the caller opts OUT), se.adr-a-lint-decides-or-defers, se.adr-applies-to-becomes-a-selector, se.adr-the-hash-is-the-pointer-the-tag-is-the-name, se.adr-install-not-zero-dep.
ALREADY SUPERSEDED IN PLACE, and left readable rather than deleted: se.adr-git-is-the-only-searcher, which carries its own account of why its conclusion fell and what survives of its analysis — including the lesson that a flip turning on someone's INTENT deserves more weight than one turning on a measurement.
